title: 応急手当（海外の資料）
note: First foreign package: universal first aid that Japan has no reusable source for (snake bites, hypothermia, frostbite, heat illness, altitude). US government manuals, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105), 'Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited'. Chosen with the source list of the Survival LLM project (github.com/anonnerdfrenzy/survival-llm, SOURCES.md, checked 2026-10-24). Only the civilian first-aid chapters; snapshots made with tool/pdf_sections.py.

sources.title: ATP 4-02.11 Casualty Response, Tactical Combat Casualty Care, and First Aid (2026), chapters 16–17
sources.note: Kept: bites (no rabies paragraph 16-6: Japan has no rabies), snakebite first aid (not the US species identification), ticks, heat and altitude injuries. Command: python3 -I tool/pdf_sections.py MANUAL.pdf OUT --from '16-1. ' --to '18-1. ' --drop-para '16-6.' --keep ... (see the snapshot's headings). Marine animals left out: its jellyfish advice (ammonia, alcohol, meat tenderizer) looks outdated; needs a medical review first.

sources.title: TC 21-3 Cold Weather Survival and Operations (2025), cold injuries
sources.note: Kept: trench foot, snow blindness, hypothermia, frostbite, dehydration, carbon monoxide. The frostbite line giving 32°F as 5.68°C (should be 0°C) is dropped.

drop_lines_containing: immediate medical help to include MEDEVAC
gaps: Text is written for soldiers ('Service member', 'Soldier', 'evacuation'); the advice itself is general first aid.
Species identification (US snakes, spiders, scorpions) left out on purpose: our rules allow universal topics only.
Translated to Japanese at build time (packages/translations/intl.firstaid.basics.ja.json); not yet reviewed by a person.

ja: 医師の診断や治療の代わりにはなりません。
米国政府の資料をLychnionが翻訳したものです。公式の訳ではなく、まだ専門家の確認を受けていません。
en: Does not replace a doctor's diagnosis or treatment.
Translated from US government manuals by Lychnion: not an official translation, not yet checked by an expert.
